newsitem.title: UK: Lonrho no comment on demerger delay report.
newsitem.headline: Lonrho no comment on demerger delay report.

text.p: Lonrho Plc on Monday declined to comment on a British newspaper report that the conglomerate's planned demerger was facing delays after a recent European Commission decision on voting rights.
The Commission earlier this month decided to bar Anglo American from voting its 28 percent stake.
The Daily Telegraph said this had prompted Lonrho to postpone sending details of the planned split-up to investors later this week.
"We don't comment on newspaper speculation," said a Lonrho spokesman. Lonrho wants to split into a trading and mining firm.
Lonrho first announced its break-up plan in January this year and has modified and delayed it several times since then.
According to the Daily Telegraph, the break-up, for which no target date has officially been announced, is hitting further delays because Anglo American upped its stake in November.
The South African mining firm raised its stake to 28 percent from 10 percent by acquiring the shares held by Lonrho's former chief executive Dieter Bock.
The European Commission earlier this month said the enlarged holding would give Anglo effective control over Lonrho, which could lead to a dominant position in the world platinum market.

The Commission also said it started a detailed investigation into Anglo's stake, which could last a maximum four months. News that Anglo would be barred from using its voting rights emerged shortly afterwards.
Anglo is meanwhile appealing to have the ban lifted for votes on matters not related to Lonrho's platinum interests.
Lonrho and Anglo are two of the world's three major platinum producers.
Together with South Africa's Gencor the two companies mine about 60 percent of the world's total output of the precious metal, used among other things in car catalysts to clean exhaust fumes.
Besides platinum, Lonrho is also a major coal and gold producer.
The company, which has a wide variety of trading operations in Africa, is in the process of selling its Princess hotel chain.
